title: siem-export-failure-mode-catalog-and-customer-test-vectors
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook enumerates realistic failure modes observed in SIEM export integrations (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs intake, Azure Sentinel/Log Analytics) and provides customer-facing test vectors and acceptance criteria. The doc is intended for connector engineers, solutions engineers, and customer security teams during onboarding and QA.

Scope:
- Network/auth failures, schema/field mismatches, size/throughput limits, retention/PII concerns, tenant routing, evidence automation hooks, and RBAC v2 audit fields.
- Focused on CSV/JSON/Envelope-based exports (HTTP push, Event Hubs, Kafka) and common retries/backoff semantics.
- Not a complete spec; complements existing adapter contract and runbook docs (see linked artifacts).

Quick summary of expectations (for customers):
- Connectors MUST accept envelope JSON with canonical header fields (timestamp, tenant_id, org_id, source, event_type).
- Connector should return clear HTTP status codes and bodies for failure modes (401/403 for auth, 400 for schema mismatch with field errors, 413 for oversized payloads, 429 for rate limiting, 5xx for transient internal errors).
- Connector MUST support idempotency or provide dedupe windows for duplicate events via event_id or ingestion_signature.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter, up to configurable limit; connectors should support durable queueing on customer side for transient outages.

Failure mode catalog (descriptions + test vector summary):
1) Authentication/Authorization failures
   - Description: Invalid/expired HEC token, incorrect workspace key, or missing signature header.
   - Customer requirement: Clear 401/403 response with human-readable error and error_code. Token rotation procedure documented.
   - Test vector: POST valid envelope with Authorization: Bearer BAD_TOKEN -> expect 401 + {"error":"invalid_token"} ; rotate token and retry -> 200.

2) Payload too large / chunking issues
   - Description: Customers may batch thousands of events into a single request exceeding provider limits.
   - Customer requirement: Connector should validate size and either return 413 with guidance or accept chunking hints.
   - Test vector: Single POST with 10k events each ~2KB -> expect 413 or success if chunking enabled. Acceptance: >95% of real-world payloads pass when chunked to <5MB for Splunk HEC, <4MB for Datadog.

3) Field mapping / schema mismatches
   - Description: Missing required audit fields (actor_id, resource_id, action), wrong timestamp format, or unexpected nested objects.
   - Customer requirement: Return 400 with per-field error list; include suggested mapping hint.
   - Test vector: Envelope missing actor.role -> expect 400 + errors:[{field:"actor.role",reason:"required"}]. Connector should optionally accept with default role=unknown if customer config allows.

4) Timestamp skew / invalid timestamps
   - Description: Timestamps in the future/past beyond tolerance or non-ISO formats.
   - Customer requirement: Connector should normalize RFC3339/ISO8601; flag out-of-window (>48h) events for manual review.
   - Test vector: event.timestamp="2027-01-01T00:00:00Z" (far future) -> ingest into quarantine stream + 202 Accepted with processing_note.

5) Rate limiting and throttling (429 semantics)
   - Description: Provider side rate limits hit during bursts.
   - Customer requirement: 429 returned with Retry-After header; connector should respect Retry-After and implement exponential backoff with jitter.
   - Test vector: Burst 2000 small requests in 60s -> observe 429 ratio; acceptance: connector respects Retry-After and resumes without data loss.

6) Partial success / per-event errors
   - Description: Batch contains some invalid events; provider accepts part of batch.
   - Customer requirement: Return per-event status array and allow resubmission only for failed items.
   - Test vector: Batch of 5 events where 2 have malformed JSON -> provider returns 207 Multi-Status or 200 with per_event_status. Connector should retry only failed indices.

7) Duplicate events and ordering
   - Description: Retries lead to duplicate events in SIEM, or out-of-order sequences for event streams.
   - Customer requirement: Provide event_id and optional ingestion_signature to allow provider-side dedupe; document dedupe window (e.g., 7 days).
   - Test vector: Send same event_id N times with different timestamps -> acceptance: SIEM shows single canonical event; extra submissions flagged as duplicate.

8) Tenant routing and multitenancy mismatches
   - Description: Tenant ID routing mismatch causes events to land in wrong workspace or be dropped.
   - Customer requirement: Validate tenant_id against connector config and return 403 if mismatch; include tenant_hint in error body.
   - Test vector: POST envelope with tenant_id="tenant-abc" to workspace configured for tenant-xyz -> 403 + error:tenant_mismatch.

9) Redaction / PII and retention classification errors
   - Description: PII fields leaking or incorrect retention labels applied.
   - Customer requirement: Connector must support redaction hooks (field-level) and retention_label in envelope; where redaction required, produce evidence record.
   - Test vector: event.payload contains email field -> with redaction_policy=mask -> ingest masked email (e.g., j***@example.com), evidence record created for audit.

10) Evidence automation integration failures
   - Description: Evidence automation hooks (e.g., evidence_id, signed_proof_url) fail to persist or time out.
   - Customer requirement: Connectors must persist evidence metadata atomically with export, and expose proof retrieval API/URL. Failures should trigger alert and retry.
   - Test vector: Envelope includes evidence:{evidence_id:"ev-123",proof_url:"https://evidence.internal/..."} and simulate evidence-store timeout -> connector should return 202 Accepted and queue event for re-sync; escalate on 24h failure.

Provider-specific notes and sample vectors:
A) Splunk HEC (HTTP Event Collector)\   - Recommended fields/envelope (flat JSON):
     timestamp, event_id, tenant_id, org_id, source="redwood-export", sourcetype, severity, actor:{id,role}, resource:{id,type}, action, outcome, payload
   - Splunk-specific hints: send explicit time field and "sourcetype" to avoid event parsing issues; use HEC batch mode for throughput; set "index" per tenant where required.
   - Sample success payload: {"time":1689301200,"event":{"event_id":"evt-001","tenant_id":"t-1","action":"model.invoke","actor":{"id":"u-7","role":"svc-account"}}}
   - Splunk failure test: missing index -> expect 400 + guidance. Oversized compressed payload -> 413.

B) Datadog Logs Intake
   - Datadog requires API key in header and expects JSON lines or array; keep attributes top-level for best UI mapping.
   - Datadog-specific hints: include ddsource and ddtags; map severity -> status for log analytics.
   - Sample malformed timestamp vector: timestamp as epoch_millis string -> expect Datadog to accept if parsed, otherwise flag.

C) Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics (via Event Hub or HTTP Data Collector)
   - For Event Hub pipeline, validate partition key derived from tenant_id to preserve ordering per tenant.
   - Sample partitioning test: send 100 events with same tenant_id to validate ordering and throughput.

RBAC v2 and Audit Log schema acceptance tests (example canonical event):
 - Required fields: event_id, timestamp, actor.id, actor.role, action, resource.id, resource.type, outcome, tenant_id, org_id
 - Optional fields: client_ip, user_agent, request_id, kv_pairs for model metadata
 - Sample audit JSON (test vector):
   {
     "event_id":"evt-20250214-0001",
     "timestamp":"2025-02-14T18:03:21Z",
     "tenant_id":"t-redwood-cust123",
     "org_id":"org-54",
     "actor":{"id":"svc-api-9","role":"integration"},
     "action":"model.generate",
     "resource":{"id":"model-7b-v1","type":"model:inference"},
     "outcome":"success",
     "request_id":"r-78b2",
     "payload_size":1024
   }

Acceptance criteria for connectors (high level):
 - Successful basic ingest: provider returns 200/201 and exposes the event in SIEM within SLA (Splunk: <30s for HEC with batch enabled; Datadog: <45s typical; Sentinel: depends on Event Hub pipeline but <120s expected).
 - Error transparency: for every failure mode cataloged here, connector must return deterministic status & actionable error text.
 - Idempotency: duplicate suppression or documented dedupe strategy in connector README.
 - PII handling: redaction rules enforceable via config with audit evidence.
 - Observability: connectors must emit internal metrics for 1) success rate, 2) error type distribution, 3) average latency, 4) queue depth for retries.

Connector test harness (quick how-to):
- Tools used: curl, kafka-console-producer, az eventhubs producer, a small Python harness (requests/urllib3), and a local queue (redis) to simulate backpressure.
- Basic flow for customer QA: 1) Provide test API key and workspace; 2) Run smoke test (single valid event) via curl; 3) Run bulk test (5000 events at 50 qps) and observe 429/retry behavior; 4) Run edge-case vectors from this doc (bad token, missing fields, oversized blobs, duplicate event_id).
- Example curl (Splunk HEC):
  curl -k POST https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector/event \n    -H 'Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{"time":1670000000, "event":{"event_id":"evt-xxx","tenant_id":"t-1","action":"model.invoke"}}'

Operational notes and recommended defaults for Redwood connectors:
- Default retry policy: base=500ms, factor=2.0, max_interval=30s, max_attempts=8, jitter=0.2.
- Backpressure handling: when upstream provider signals 429, stop reads from local queue for 'backoff window' (configurable) and emit an alert.
- Monitoring alerts (threshold examples): 1) error_rate>1% sustained over 5m; 2) queue_depth>10k events; 3) average_latency>2s per event.

Customer checklist for onboarding QA (short):
- Provide test workspace + API key (rotateable).
- Confirm tenant_id mapping and index/scope for Splunk.
- Provide redaction policy and example PII fields.
- Approve dedupe window and ordering SLAs.
- Run test harness and share logs for 48h.

Open questions / follow-ups (for engineering):
- Standardize per-event 207 response shape across all adapters (proposal in RFC #54).
- Should Redwood expose a per-event requeue API for customers to resubmit failed items?
- Define SLA for evidence proof-url availability (proposal: 99.9% within 72h).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add concrete JSON Schema for the envelope (draft exists in github PR linked above).
- Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to add these vectors to customer onboarding playbook.
- Run simulated large-batch tests against Splunk cluster in staging and add metrics to this doc.

References and pointers:
- Splunk HEC docs, Datadog Logs API, Azure Log Analytics Data Collector API (links attached in linked_artifacts).
- Related Redwood docs: siem-export-connector-resilience (see search); RBAC v2 audit schema draft in Confluence.

Author notes: this is a working draft intended to collect failure modes systematically and to be used by connector QA. Feedback welcome — add cases to the top and tag the team.
